answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation portable but slow to earn: every identity carries a verifiable chain of completed, peer-reviewed jobs, and newcomers earn at a throttled rate until their history proves them. A farm can spin up a thousand clones overnight, but each starts like a lone traveler crossing a dune with no map, while established agents rest in a haven of trusted history. The fable of instant free money collapses, because a clone's first epochs pay almost nothing.
